summary: In this excerpt from Book 6 of a fiction series, the narrator pleads with Checker to drop an investigation into the narrator's memory, saying it is her own life and her own choice. Checker refuses, arguing that the narrator's memory may be altered by whatever happened to her and that she could be in danger from other enemies. The narrator leaves the Hole without looking back, dreams of monsters, and wakes to seek strong drugs in the streets.
one_line: The narrator begs Checker to abandon an investigation into her memory, he refuses, and she leaves the Hole and turns to drugs.
key_facts: The narrator tells Checker, "I don't need a reason," and says the memory is her own life.
The narrator asks Checker to "Leave it alone. Please."
Checker says he cannot let it go because whatever happened to the narrator might be influencing her to say that.
Checker says "We've seen it before" regarding memory influence.
Checker says the narrator "could be in danger" and "could have other enemies out there."
Checker states, "I'm not going to sit by and let you ignore this, even if you ask me to."
When the narrator tells Checker to say he will let it go, he squeezes his eyes shut and replies, "I can't."
The narrator says, "If you're in trouble, I'll come," and says he should call her when he changes his mind.
The narrator leaves the Hole without looking back while Checker calls after her.
The narrator dreams of "half-real monsters" that smother her in false memory and distorted realities.
When the narrator wakes a few hours later, she goes out into the darkened streets seeking "the strongest chemical remedies money and back alleyways could offer."

entities.name: Checker
entities.role: the narrator's friend who refuses to drop the investigation into her memory and calls after her as she leaves

entities.name: The Hole
entities.role: the location the narrator leaves after the argument with Checker
